method: Compare each country's annual wind total across the sources that report it. The reference is the national figure where one exists for the whole wind fleet over the calendar year: a national source read live, or a figure taken from the national publisher's own report, quoted and linked. A series that covers only part of the fleet, such as Great Britain's transmission-metered wind, or a fiscal year, is compared but never used as the reference. Where there is no such national figure, the reference is Eurostat's gross electricity production, and outside Eurostat's countries Ember. A national figure is only as good as its publisher: it can be preliminary, and it can draw the country's borders differently from the international compilers. The bands follow the PyVWF scorecard audit: a ratio within 0.85-1.15 of the reference agrees, 0.70-1.30 is noted, and anything further out is flagged. Gross production runs above what transmission operators meter, so ratios a little under 1 are normal; the entry's traps usually say why. Fleets under 0.05 TWh a year are compared but not judged, because rounding alone moves their ratio. Ember and Eurostat compile national figures, so an exact match can mean the same upstream data rather than independent confirmation; the check catches a series that measures only part of a fleet, not a shared error.

reference.name: CEB
reference.why: CEB counts its own Mannar farm (104 MW) and the private farms (163 MW) as "NCRE - Wind". The 2024 gross generation table gives Mannar 387.997 GWh less 5.023 GWh station use, plus private wind 409.027 GWh, which is 792.0 GWh net: the whole grid fleet.
